ai.title: Add count-edit-file script for 24h edit metrics
ai.summary: New internal tooling script scripts/count-edit-file.ts added. It queries the message table for entries finished in last 24 hours. Counts occurrences of '</edit_file>' in responses to derive edit volume metrics.

eli5.text: A new internal tool now quietly tallies how often people make 24-hour edits to files in the system, giving the team a way to measure that activity without touching the product itself. If you opened the company's internal scripts folder, you'd see a small TypeScript program that searches the last day's records for edit-file actions and reports total edits, how many messages included edits, and the average edits per message. The script is live and functional for internal teams who need the metric, but regular users won't see or interact with it.

ai.title: LRU cache added for token counting
ai.summary: LRU cache added to token counting. New common/src/util/lru-cache.ts provides generic LRUCache class. backend/src/util/token-counter.ts caches results for strings >100 chars, max 10k entries. Reduces repeated gpt-tokenizer encode calls.

eli5.text: When the assistant counts how many tokens are in your long messages, it now remembers recent answers instead of recomputing them every time. Each time you send a message longer than 100 characters, the system checks if it has already calculated the token count for that exact text, and if so returns the stored result immediately. It keeps this memory limited to about 10,000 recent messages, automatically forgetting the oldest ones to make room. The whole thing is live today and you would notice it as slightly faster and more consistent response times when working with repeated or similar chunks of text.

ai.title: Estimate file tree pruning to avoid repeated token counts
ai.summary: Replaced iterative deep-file removal with sampled token estimation in `backend/src/truncate-file-tree.ts`. `getFilesWithDepths` collects files; `sampleSize` picks 30 files to compute `avgTokensPerFileName`; `estimatedFilesToRemove` calculates bulk removal count. This avoids expensive `countTokensJson` calls in the `while` loop, speeding up pruning. `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` passes `fileTreeTokenBudget` to support the new logic.

eli5.text: When the assistant works with a large list of files, it used to check each file one at a time to decide which ones to remove when it ran low on space. Now it looks at a small sample of files, estimates how much each file roughly adds to the total size, and removes a batch all at once. If you use the assistant and your project has many files, trimming the file list happens faster instead of one-by-one.

ai.title: Add duration to system prompt logs
ai.summary: Added `duration` field to system prompt logs in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. `getSearchSystemPrompt` and `getAgentSystemPrompt` now record `Date.now() - startTime` in their log metadata. This change provides visibility into prompt construction time for both search and agent flows. Scope limited to backend logging internals.

eli5.text: When the assistant is getting ready to answer your question, the system now quietly records how long that setup work takes. If you were looking at the internal logs, you'd see a new timing number attached to both search-style and agent-style prompt construction, so teams can spot when prompt building is slower than expected. It's already live and only affects internal logging, so nothing about your experience changes.

ai.title: Disable project filetree prompt in agent system prompt
ai.summary: Commented out `getProjectFileTreePrompt` call and its inclusion in `getAgentSystemPrompt` in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. Removes filetree from agent context window. Internal refactor.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer sees a map of your project files before it starts answering. Previously, every time the assistant prepared to respond, it loaded a full directory listing into its context, which consumed tokens and processing time. The directory listing is now turned off, so the assistant begins work without that file-tree reference attached to its prompt. Internal tools confirm the change is in place and live. If you reviewed the prompt the assistant builds, you would notice the section that once included the project file tree is now commented out.

ai.title: Add debug logs and lower slow-truncation threshold
ai.summary: Added granular `logger.debug` calls at each truncation stage (A, unimportant-files, tokens, depth-based) in `backend/src/truncate-file-tree.ts` to track token budget adherence and duration. Lowered the warning threshold for slow file name truncation and pruning from 300ms to 100ms. Minor formatting updates applied to arrow functions and line breaks.

ai.title: Add iteration and progress guards to truncate-file-tree loop
ai.summary: truncateFileTreeBasedOnTokenBudget in backend/src/truncate-file-tree.ts adds MAX_ITERATIONS=10 and a previousTokenCount check to prevent infinite loops during token-budget truncation. The loop now breaks early if currentTokenCount >= previousTokenCount, logging a warning via logger.warn. Scope is backend only; no user-facing surfaces change. Iteration count and token deltas are logged when the guard trips.

eli5.text: When the system tries to shrink a project file list to fit a token budget, it now stops itself if it gets stuck not making progress, so it can no longer spin forever on the same files. This is a behind-the-scenes safety adjustment for a backend process that trims file lists; no front-facing features change for people using the product. Today, the change is live and in effect, but you would not notice it unless the trimming process was about to hang and it now stops after ten passes or when removing more files stops lowering the token count.

ai.title: Added troubleshooting help page

eli5.text: A new troubleshooting guide has been added to the help section, showing users where their chat history is stored on their computer and offering solutions for common connection errors. The FAQ page was also updated to make the data storage explanation easier to understand.

ai.title: Browser runner stops restarting on execution failure
ai.summary: Removed automatic browser restart logic in `npm-app/src/browser-runner.ts` when execution fails. Previously, `BrowserRunner` attempted to recover by calling `shutdown` followed by `startBrowser` for non-stop actions. Now, the runner simply shuts down and rethrows the error.

eli5.text: When the browser-based assistant failed during a task, it previously tried to fix itself by restarting the browser and resuming. Now, it simply stops and reports the failure instead of attempting recovery. This affects the internal tooling used to run browser-based tasks, making failures more predictable and easier to debug.

ai.title: Moved troubleshooting docs to advanced
ai.summary: Renamed `web/src/content/help/troubleshooting.mdx` to `web/src/content/advanced/troubleshooting.mdx`. This reorganization shifts troubleshooting guidance into the advanced content section. Scope limited to the Web docs directory structure.

eli5.text: The troubleshooting help pages have been moved from the general help section into the advanced section of the website. This is a behind-the-scenes reorganization that only affects where the documentation lives, not what it says. You would only notice this if you were looking for troubleshooting content and found it under the advanced help area instead of the regular help section.

ai.title: Fix banner mobile layout
ai.summary: Banner layout adjusted for mobile via `web/src/components/ui/banner.tsx`. Container padding moved from outer div to inner container; text wrapping changed to `md:whitespace-nowrap`. Gift icon set to `flex-shrink-0` to prevent compression.

eli5.text: When you visit the site on a phone, the blue announcement bar at the top now keeps its text on one line instead of wrapping awkwardly, and the small gift icon next to it stays its normal size rather than getting squished. The padding that spaces the text away from the edges was moved so it works better on narrow screens. If you open the site on a mobile device, the banner text no longer breaks into multiple lines and stays neatly aligned with even spacing.

ai.title: ensureUrlProtocol normalizes missing scheme in browser and scraper
ai.summary: Added ensureUrlProtocol in common/src/util/string.ts to inject http:// for localhost/127.0.0.1 and https:// for other domains. Applied to npm-app/src/browser-runner.ts page.goto and npm-app/src/web-scraper.ts scrapeWebPage to prevent navigation failures on scheme-less URLs. Scope limited to shared string utility and npm-app browser/scraping surfaces.

eli5.text: If you gave the app a web address like "example.com" without typing "https://" first, it used to fail and you would see an error or a blank screen. Now the app quietly adds the missing "https://" (or "http://" for local addresses) behind the scenes before loading the page, so you land on the site instead of an error. This fix applies whenever the app opens a web page in its built-in browser for tasks like browsing or scraping content.

ai.title: Update continue prompt in main-prompt.ts
ai.summary: The `continue` tool input in `main-prompt.ts` now explicitly instructs the agent to summarize and review implementation without re-calling `plan_complex_change`. This change prevents the agent from entering a loop with the planning tool. The update affects the backend core logic in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes a task and reviews its own work, it now explicitly avoids asking the planning tool to start over. This prevents the assistant from getting stuck in a loop where it keeps re-planning instead of moving forward. You'd notice the assistant wrapping up its review and improvements directly instead of restarting the planning step.

ai.title: Version 1.0.154
ai.summary: Freebuff version 1.0.154 released. Internal version bump in npm-app/package.json. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The app's internal version number was bumped from 1.0.153 to 1.0.154, which means it's now officially running the latest build that includes a handful of behind-the-scenes improvements: a small script that tracks how many file edits happen within 24 hours, an LRU cache that speeds up token counting, and more accurate file tree pruning to avoid repeated counting work. These changes are part of the new release and are now active, although most users won't notice a direct difference, they're mostly internal tweaks to keep the app stable and up to date. If you were to look, you'd see the updated version label reflecting all the minor fixes and optimizations shipped since the last version.

ai.title: Handle null filepaths in getFiles
ai.summary: Added null/empty check for file paths in getFiles. Prevents crashes when invalid paths are passed. Change applies to npm-app/src/project-files.ts.

eli5.text: The system now safely skips over any file entries that come through without a proper name or location, instead of stopping or failing when it encounters one. If you were watching the tool process a list of files, you'd see those empty entries get set aside with a clear label rather than causing the whole operation to crash. It is live today and applies whenever the file-handling step runs behind the scenes.

ai.title: Update troubleshooting docs
ai.summary: Simplified connection troubleshooting steps in `troubleshooting.mdx`. Removed `codebuff auth status` check and updated login/logout commands to `logout` and `login`. Clarified support response times, noting subscribers are prioritized but replies occur within a week.

eli5.text: The instructions people follow when something stops connecting have been simplified: one step that asked you to run a separate check is gone, and the steps for signing out and back in now read as plain 'logout' and 'login' instead of longer commands. The part about getting help from support now says subscribers are prioritized but a reply usually comes within a week. If you looked, you'd see a shorter, two-step list under connection troubles and a clearer line about how fast paying users hear back. The change is live today in the troubleshooting documentation.

ai.title: Cap planning file tokens at 140k
ai.summary: Added `loadFilesForPlanning` in `backend/src/planning.ts` to filter fetched files before planning. Drops entries with `null` content, `[INVALID_FILE_PATH]`, or >40k tokens, then removes files exceeding 140k cumulative tokens. Refactored `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to use this helper instead of inline filtering. Reduced `TOKEN_COUNT_CACHE` size from 10k to 5k in `backend/src/util/token-counter.ts` to bound memory.

eli5.text: When the assistant prepares to make code changes, it now stops reading files that are missing content, unreadable, or larger than 40,000 tokens, and caps the total amount it pulls in for planning at 140,000 tokens. If you use the coding assistant today, very large or broken files won't be loaded into its working memory when it forms a plan, so it won't try to analyze or include file sections beyond that 140,000-token ceiling. The 140,000-token limit is now live for anyone triggering a planning session that pulls in multiple files.

ai.title: Browser action prompt tweaks
ai.summary: System prompt for `browser_action` tool updated in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. Instructions clarify that the agent must never start the user's development server, emphasizing explicit user action for server startup. The prompt structure removes redundant error handling sections and reinforces the `<tool_call name="browser_action">` XML prefix requirement.

eli5.text: From 2025-02-05, the system that helps navigate and inspect websites now follows stricter instructions: it will never launch your development server for you. Instead, if it detects that no server is running, it will provide you with written steps to start it yourself in a new window. This change affects anyone asking the assistant to open or test a web page that requires a locally hosted server. If you looked at the assistant's behavior, you would notice it no longer attempts to start your server automatically; it only offers guidance when it sees the server is not running.

ai.title: Re-enable filetree in agent system prompt
ai.summary: Uncomments `getProjectFileTreePrompt` and `countTokensJson` calls in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. The agent now includes the project file tree in the system prompt again, constrained by `fileTreeTokenBudget` (5k for lite, 20k otherwise). This reverts a previous disablement, restoring file context visibility for the agent.

eli5.text: The AI assistant inside the coding tool will once again be able to see a map of your project's files when it is deciding what code to write or change. The system had temporarily turned this file map back on, and that feature is now active, letting the assistant understand your project structure as it works. If you watched the AI at work, you might notice it gives answers that take more of your project's files into account, instead of working in the dark.
